items.title: Democratic socialist Nithya Raman wins LA mayoral race
items.feedTitle: Nithya Raman ousts incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles mayor's race, CBS News projects
items.summary: Nithya Raman, a Democratic Socialist backed by the DSA, has defeated incumbent Karen Bass in Los Angeles' mayoral election. Raman becomes the city's first South Asian mayor and will lead the second-largest U.S. city. Her victory, along with New York's similar result, means America's two most populous cities will now be led by democratic socialists. Raman has pledged action on homelessness and affordable housing.

items.title: Washington voters ban transgender girls in school sports
items.feedTitle: Washington voters approve transgender athlete ban
items.summary: Washington state voters have approved a ballot measure to reverse the state's long-standing policy allowing transgender girls to compete on girls' and women's school sports teams. The measure requires students to submit healthcare provider documentation verifying their sex. This represents a significant policy reversal in a Democratic-leaning state and reflects ongoing national tensions over transgender rights in athletics.

items.title: Democrat Jessica Killin flips Colorado GOP House seat
items.feedTitle: Democrat Jessica Killin flips longtime GOP-held Colorado House seat
items.summary: Democrat Jessica Killin has defeated GOP Rep. Jeff Crank in Colorado's 5th Congressional District, marking a historic Democratic first for the Colorado Springs-area district. The seat had never elected a Democrat since its creation in 1973. Killin's victory is part of a broader Democratic surge in traditionally Republican areas during the midterm elections.

items.title: Meta, TikTok, Google sue California over child safety law
items.feedTitle: Meta, TikTok, Google sue California over child online safety restrictions
items.summary: Meta, TikTok, and Google have filed separate lawsuits challenging California's new 'Digital Age Assurance Act,' which takes effect January 1. The companies argue the law restricts child access to social media and violates their First Amendment rights. The bipartisan legislation aims to tighten restrictions on children's social media usage, setting the stage for a major legal battle over tech regulation.

stlouis.title: Two Black St. Louis-area lawmakers join House leadership
stlouis.feedTitle: Two Black St. Louis area lawmakers join House leadership
stlouis.summary: Two Black lawmakers from the St. Louis metro area have been selected for House leadership positions following Democrats' midterm victories. The appointments reflect the region's increased political influence and the Democratic Party's focus on diverse representation in leadership roles.

stlouis.title: Missouri Amendment 8 forces statewide sheriff elections
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri's Amendment 8 narrowly passes, forces sheriff elections everywhere except St. Louis and St. Charles counties
stlouis.summary: Missouri voters narrowly approved Amendment 8, which will require sheriff elections statewide, with the exception of St. Louis and St. Charles counties. The measure marks a significant change to how sheriffs are selected in the state and reflects ongoing debates over local governance structures.

stlouis.title: St. Louis County voters prioritize affordability for 2028
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis County voters say Democrats need to focus on affordability for 2028
stlouis.summary: Polling of St. Louis County voters conducted after the midterms shows Democrats must focus on affordability and cost-of-living concerns heading into 2028. The survey reflects broad voter anxiety about economic pressures and suggests that Democrats' midterm success may not translate into lasting support without addressing these kitchen-table issues.

items.title: Iran's security chief meets Putin, discusses regional security
items.feedTitle: Iran’s security chief meets Putin, delivers message from Khamenei
items.summary: Iran's top security official has met with President Putin in Moscow to discuss regional security and deliver a message from Khamenei. The meeting underscores deepening coordination between Iran and Russia amid heightened tensions over potential U.S. military strikes on Iran. The closed-door talks signal both countries' efforts to coordinate responses to escalating regional conflicts.

items.title: Trump sees Ukraine peace deal as 'very close
items.feedTitle: Trump says Russia-Ukraine deal is near after meeting Putin’s envoy
items.summary: Trump says he met with Putin's envoy at the White House and sees a Russia-Ukraine peace deal as 'very close,' though he provided no specifics. Trump did not meet with visiting Ukrainian officials despite their presence at the White House. First Lady Melania Trump hosted both Russian and Ukrainian representatives at a meeting focused on a localized ceasefire. The claims lack independent verification of progress.

items.title: Hoax bomb threats disrupt 27+ European flights
items.feedTitle: Hoax bomb threats force emergency landings, evacuations across Europe
items.summary: Hoax bomb threats have caused disruptions to at least 27 flights across Europe, forcing emergency landings and evacuations at multiple airports. Official sources describe the threats as 'malicious hoaxes' but note no credible evidence yet links them to Russia, Iran, or any state actor. The incidents represent the second such wave of hoax threats within a week, raising concerns about hybrid warfare tactics.

items.title: Paraguay president resigns after bank collapse crisis
items.feedTitle: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
items.summary: Paraguayan President Santiago Peña has resigned following the collapse of a major digital bank that froze millions of people's savings. The banking scandal triggered both his resignation and an impeachment process after prosecutors announced criminal investigations. The crisis represents a significant political upheaval in South America and raises questions about financial oversight in the region.

items.title: Bank of England raises rates to 4% after three years
items.feedTitle: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%, the first increase for more than three years
items.summary: The Bank of England has raised its base rate to 4% for the first time in over three years, increasing from 3.75%. The governor signaled another rate hike may follow soon as the central bank battles rising inflation. The move comes amid a cost-of-living crisis in the UK and raises concerns about the impact on households already struggling with expenses.

items.title: Delhi's toxic air returns as winter pollution season begins
items.feedTitle: Delhi's toxic winter air is back - is the Indian capital prepared for pollution?
items.summary: Delhi's winter air quality has deteriorated sharply as toxic pollution returns to the capital ahead of Diwali. The government has announced a four-month winter action plan, but experts warn it may be insufficient to combat the seasonal spike. The pollution crisis combines factors including farm fires, firecrackers, and winter weather conditions, creating a public health emergency.

items.title: Jaypal Malviya secures India's Olympic shooting quota
items.feedTitle: Jaypal Malviya secures India's first Olympic quota in shooting after clinching silver in men's 10m air pistol event at the ISSF World Championship. 🇮🇳💪🔫 Silver Medal 🥈 Olympic Quota ✅ 📸 NRAI
items.summary: Shooter Jaypal Malviya has won India's first Olympic quota in shooting after claiming a silver medal in the men's 10m air pistol event at the ISSF World Championship. The achievement represents a significant milestone for Indian shooting ahead of the 2028 Olympics. Malviya's success underscores India's growing strength in marksmanship on the international stage.

items.title: Air India resumes US flights via Iraq airspace
items.feedTitle:
Air India re-starts direct flights to US
from Mumbai, Delhi via Iraq airspace - The New Indian Express
items.summary: Air India has restarted direct flights to the United States from Mumbai and Delhi, utilizing Iraq airspace for the route. The resumption of direct transatlantic service marks an expansion of Air India's international network and reflects improved regional security conditions. The new routing provides a more efficient path for India-U.S. travel.

items.title: India successfully test-fires Pralay quasi-ballistic missile
items.feedTitle: India successfully test-fires indigenously developed quasi-ballistic missile Pralay | Watch | India News
items.summary: India has successfully conducted a flight test of the indigenously developed Pralay quasi-ballistic missile. The test demonstrates India's growing capability in advanced defense systems and missile technology. The achievement underscores India's commitment to self-reliance in defense manufacturing and strategic deterrence.

items.title: Three UNESCO-listed works add to India's literary heritage
items.feedTitle: Three more works of India’s literary and intellectual heritage added in UNESCO’s list
items.summary: Three additional works of India's literary and intellectual heritage have been added to UNESCO's Memory of the World register. The recognition highlights India's rich cultural and intellectual traditions and validates centuries of scholarly work. The additions strengthen India's cultural standing on the global stage.

immigration.title: Democratic Congress control raises H-1B visa hopes
immigration.feedTitle: Democratic Control of Congress Could Reshape H-1B Visa Policy and U.S.-India Trade Relations
immigration.summary: With Democrats taking control of Congress following midterm victories, Indian H-1B visa holders and tech workers are hopeful for potential scrutiny of recent visa restrictions and fee increases. Democratic lawmakers have signaled interest in reviewing H-1B policies that were tightened under Republican administration. However, legal experts caution that immediate relief is unlikely, as any changes would require time to navigate the legislative process and potential Trump administration opposition.

immigration.title: DHS finalizes automatic EAD extension removal, finalized and in effect
immigration.feedTitle: Removal of Automatic Extensions for Certain Employment Authorization Documents
immigration.summary: DHS published a final interim rule on October 30, 2025, ending automatic extensions for employment authorization documents (I-766 forms, EADs) for applicants who have timely filed renewal applications. The rule, finalized and now in effect, forces applicants with pending cases to reapply or face gaps in work authorization. This policy significantly impacts millions of immigrants, particularly H-1B and family-based visa holders with pending green card applications.

immigration.title: USCIS proposes removing deference to prior visa approvals, proposed not final
immigration.feedTitle: Removing Deference to Prior USCIS Determinations of Eligibility
immigration.summary: USCIS has proposed removing 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which currently provides deference to prior approvals when adjudicating extension requests for work visa petitions. The proposed rule, not yet finalized, would increase scrutiny of H-1B and L-1 visa renewals even when circumstances remain unchanged. This proposal would make it harder for employers to predictably extend visas and could disproportionately affect Indian tech workers in the U.S.

items.title: Nasdaq suffers worst day in 18 months after midterms
items.feedTitle: Midterms boost for global markets | Hindustan Times
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite plummeted 5.5% on November 5 in its worst single day in 18 months, erasing post-election gains and wiping nearly $2 trillion from the index. AI and semiconductor stocks were hammered as investors feared Democratic control of Congress could trigger tougher regulation of data centers and AI development. Major tech indices fell sharply, with the S&P 500 down 4.4% and the Dow falling 1,833 points, extending a broader global rout.

items.title: Oil price falls amid Iran war resolution hopes
items.feedTitle: Oil price falls amid hope of a breakthrough to end Iran war
items.summary: Brent crude has fallen to its lowest level in over two weeks, dropping more than 6.5% to $105.55 per barrel on hopes of a potential breakthrough to end the Iran war. The price decline reflects investor relief over the possibility of de-escalation in the Middle East and reduced regional tensions. Oil prices remain sensitive to any developments regarding U.S.-Iran military action.

items.title: Sensex gains 6,064 points in six sessions
items.feedTitle: Sensex up 6,064 pts in six days; eyes strongest pre-Diwali rally in 35 yrs
items.summary: India's Sensex index surged 6,064 points over six consecutive trading sessions, posting its strongest pre-Diwali rally in 35 years. The rally was fueled by foreign fund inflows of Rs 14,975 crore as overseas investors responded positively to the Democratic midterm wave. Nifty broke above 24,500 and hit three-month highs, driven by financial stocks and renewed investor appetite for equities.

items.feedTitle: Oil Drops Sharply but Middle East Supply Concerns Support Prices
items.summary: Oil prices have fallen sharply following the midterm elections amid hopes for de-escalation in the Iran conflict, yet concerns about Middle East supply disruptions continue to provide underlying support. Brent crude and WTI are volatile as markets weigh geopolitical risks against softer global demand. The price decline reflects competing forces of improved diplomatic prospects and persistent regional tensions.

cards.title: Momentum over motivation
cards.insight: Voting patterns and market behavior show that momentum—the repeated reinforcement of a behavior through small wins—outweighs initial motivation. Voter turnout surged not from grand ideological speeches, but from sustained local organizing that made participation habitual. Markets, too, follow momentum: a six-day rally built conviction despite underlying volatility.
cards.takeaway: Build one small win per day into your habit change, no matter how tiny. The accumulation matters more than the size.

cards.title: Friction as friend, not foe
cards.insight: California's Newsom faced bureaucratic friction to grant clemency (548 individual reviews), yet the friction itself became a safeguard. Similarly, Washington voters added friction to trans athlete eligibility (healthcare provider documentation), embedding verification into the process. Friction slows impulsive reversals and makes habits sticky.
cards.takeaway: When designing a new habit, add one small friction point—not to discourage, but to make the behavior deliberate and memorable.

cards.title: Social permission unlocks private change
cards.insight: OpenAI's shift on data center NDAs and local input came not from internal conviction but from public permission—voter rejection and Democratic sweeps gave dissent legitimacy. Investors suddenly felt free to doubt Anthropic's $1.5T valuation once the political climate shifted. People change behaviors when they see permission from peers or authority.
cards.takeaway: Before changing a habit alone, find or create a group norm that makes the new behavior feel socially acceptable—peer permission accelerates private transformation.

cards.title: Identity precedes habit
cards.insight: Democratic victories didn't change policy overnight; they changed how people saw themselves. A voter who elected progressives to Congress may now self-identify differently, which subtly reshapes daily choices on energy, tech, and community. Habits stick when they align with identity, not willpower.
cards.takeaway: Anchor your habit change to a new identity label ('I'm someone who...') rather than relying on discipline. Your brain will work harder to stay consistent with who you've decided to be.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO valuation faces $500B hit after tech rout
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic’s IPO timing threatened by AI backlash, historic tech rout
ai.summary: Anthropic's planned IPO has faced investor skepticism following the market collapse, with major investors expressing doubt that the AI startup can achieve its previously targeted $1.5 trillion valuation. The company's IPO timing has been threatened by broader AI backlash and the historic tech stock selloff after the midterm elections. Potential investors are pushing for lower valuations as concerns grow about AI regulation under a Democratic Congress.

ai.title: OpenAI pledges greater local input on data centers
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI makes new data center commitments, AI policy recommendations
ai.summary: OpenAI has announced it will change how it handles data center projects, pledging to give local communities more say in decision-making and stepping back from NDAs that previously silenced opposition. The commitment comes after widespread outcry and political backlash against AI infrastructure projects during the midterm elections. OpenAI's policy shift reflects growing recognition that data center opposition crossed party lines and poses regulatory risks.

ai.title: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber for vulnerability research
ai.feedTitle: OpenAI launches GPT-6 Cyber with stronger exploit research and higher API price than Anthropic and Google
ai.summary: OpenAI has launched GPT-6 Cyber, a specialized model designed to identify and research software vulnerabilities and security exploits. The model found 81 high-severity flaws in Firefox and helps developers patch security issues before malicious actors can exploit them. The cybersecurity-focused model comes as AI labs face increased scrutiny over their role in protecting digital infrastructure.

ai.title: Anthropic accelerating AI development amid slowdown calls
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic is rapidly accelerating AI development amid slowdown calls, outside research group says
ai.summary: External research group METR reports that Anthropic has nearly doubled its model capability growth rate, rapidly advancing AI development even as outside voices call for industry slowdowns. The acceleration contradicts calls from some quarters for more measured development and comes amid heightened debate over AI regulation following Democratic midterm victories. Anthropic's pace underscores competitive pressure within the AI industry.

ai.title: Meta warns data center opposition could limit AI expansion
ai.feedTitle: Meta warns that election backlash against data centers could make AI expansion harder
ai.summary: Meta has cautioned that growing political opposition to data centers could threaten future AI infrastructure investments, highlighting the midterm backlash as a material business risk. The company's warning reflects widespread community and political pushback against massive data center projects needed for AI development. Meta's concerns underscore how the midterm results have created regulatory and political headwinds for AI industry buildout plans.
